title: Miniature
description: A night photograph of Times Square with its depth, shown as a print. The pointer is the plane of focus: hover over herb, a taxi or a far billboard and the lens racks to that distance through the real depth of the street, a gently reverse-tilted plane that blurs top and bottom faster than any real lens at this scale would, until the city reads as a model of itself. The neon opens into soft discs and foreground blur spills over what sits behind it, never the other way. Click to hold focus.
intent: After Olivo Barbieri's site specific_ city photographs (https://www.olivobarbieri.it/) and Vincent Laforet's tilt-shift aerials (https://laforetvisuals.com/): depth of field that is physically wrong for the scale, driven by a Depth Anything V2 map of herb's own photo. Circle of confusion is proportional to the gap in inverse depth, gathered at reduced resolution with occlusion-aware scatter-as-gather and a depth-aware joint upsample.
